title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
This is a perception and response failure in an autonomous driving system. The vehicle was operating in autonomous mode on a residential street when it struck a duck that was nesting in a pot outside a restaurant. It did not slow down or stop afterward. The object in its path was small, stationary, and outside the ordinary traffic the system was built to handle, and the system did not treat it as an obstacle requiring a response.

The failure sits at the detection stage, and the human check that existed did not catch it either. A safety operator was present in the vehicle, which is the fallback the deployment relied on, and the vehicle still hit the duck without the operator intervening in time. Catching this would have required either the perception system to classify a small animal as something to avoid, or the operator to notice and take over before the impact. Avride's response was geographic rather than technical at first, excluding certain streets around the lake from its testing area, alongside simulation work on the underlying technology.

What is not established is the resident claim that the vehicle also failed to stop at a stop sign. Avride disputed that account after reviewing vehicle data and replaying the scene in simulation, and no finding on the question has been reported. The reports also do not establish what the vehicle's sensors registered in the moments before the collision.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
An autonomous vehicle operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community concern. The incident occurred when the self-driving car, which had a human safety operator present, hit the duck without slowing down or stopping afterward. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, making it familiar to residents and intensifying their reaction. A neighborhood resident also claimed the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, though Avride disputed this assertion after reviewing vehicle data and replaying the scene in simulation.

Following the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating in autonomous mode and announced it would adjust its testing area by excluding certain streets around the lake. The company is now conducting controlled simulation experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations while ensuring safety performance remains unaffected. Local residents have preserved the duck's eggs in an incubator. Meanwhile, other autonomous vehicle companies including Waymo, Tesla, and Zoox also operate in Austin.
